chunks.content: ## Creating a Flat Knot Effect on a T-Shirt in CLO This section explains how to create a flat knot effect on the bottom front of a T-shirt using CLO’s simulation and pattern tools. Key terms include board particles, fixing pins, elasticity settings, and simulation adjustments. ### Preparing the T-Shirt and Setting Board Particles - Open the T-shirt project file in CLO. - The knot will be created on the front bottom side of the T-shirt. - Set the **board particles** parameter to **10** to control the fabric simulation detail. - Since the knot is on one side, remove the left and right sides of the front and the left side of the back pattern pieces. - Ensure the 3D window displays the T-shirt surface with the right and left sides of the clear board positioned opposite each other. ### Marking the Knot Area - At the knot position on the bottom front of the T-shirt, use CLO’s internal tool to draw a circle with a **200 mm diameter**. - Add a small **fixing pin** at the bottom of this circle to anchor the fabric during simulation. ### Simulating the Initial Knot Lift - Enter **simulation mode**. - Lift the T-shirt from the bottom at the knot area. - Manually pull the fabric as needed to prevent mesh penetration or distortion during lifting. - After lifting, close the simulation and remove the opposite side of the T-shirt pattern to focus on the knot area. ### Adjusting the Inner Circle and Applying Elasticity - Switch to the **T-shirt locking tool**. - Select the inner circle line around the knot area. - Pull the grid points of the inner circle outward slightly to enlarge its diameter to about **210 mm**. - Adjust the circle position to fully encompass the fixing pin. - Apply elasticity to the inner circle line with these settings: - **Elasticity intensity:** 90 - **Proportion:** 5 ### Simulating the Knot Binding - Start the simulation with the elasticity applied. - The fabric behaves like a rubber band, binding around the fixing pin to create the knot effect. - Delete the fixing pin inside the circle to allow the fabric to settle. - Restart the simulation to observe the knot forming with the tied inner circle fabric. - The knot appears reversed on the front side, showing the tied effect. ### Refining the Knot Shape - Turn off the simulation to review the knot state. - Delete the fixing pin at the bottom row. - Restart simulation and use manual adjustments (small hand tool) to pull and rearrange fabric for a natural knot shape. - Continue simulating and adjusting until the knot shape is satisfactory. ### Finalizing the T-Shirt Knot - Improve the clothing quality by adjusting fabric tension and fit. - If the knot area (circle) is unstable, sew the left and right sides of the circle to secure it. - Simulate again to confirm stability. - After the final simulation, close the simulation mode.
